title: PhD in Quantum Physics - Rare-earth Ion Single Photon Emitter at TU Delft, Netherlands

organization.about: TU Delft is a public technical university in Delft, the Netherlands. It offers undergraduate, master's and doctoral education across engineering, architecture, design and applied sciences. Its research connects technical knowledge with practical challenges, including energy, mobility, infrastructure and sustainability, through collaboration with industry, public organisations and international academic institutions worldwide.

intro: Fully funded TU Delft PhD in the Groeblacher Lab on highly coherent single photon emitters using erbium ions in the telecom C-band for the quantum internet. Deadline: 8 November 2026. Applicants can apply without IELTS - selection is based on documents and an English interview, not a test certificate.
description:
Project Overview

Can silicon play a critical role in building the next generation of the internet - the quantum internet? To realise a fully functional and scalable quantum network, the Groeblacher Lab is developing highly coherent single photon emitters using erbium ions operating in the telecom C-band and directly embedded in a solid-state crystal such as silicon.

The project realises high-quality light-matter interfaces and directly enhances photon emission into an optical channel using photonic crystal cavities. By leveraging different isotopes for long-lived and programmable quantum registers, the team plans to realise all the critical parts of a quantum network using fully integrated and highly scalable structures.

Research Areas

  • Rare-earth ion physics and single emitters in solid-state systems
  • Photonic crystal cavities for enhanced photon emission
  • Experimental AMO and quantum optics techniques
  • Finite-element simulation and advanced computer-based experimentation

Funding and Employment

Employment and financial support
ComponentDetails
PositionPaid doctoral employee (full-time, 38 hours/week)
SalaryEUR 3,204 to EUR 4,051 gross per month, increasing from the first to the fourth year, based on the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities (CAO).
Additional pay8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% end-of-year bonus.
DurationFour years in principle, split into two contracts: an initial 18-month contract with a go/no-go assessment, followed by 30 months after a satisfactory assessment.
TrainingEnrolment in the TU Delft Graduate School, including the Doctoral Education Programme with supervision and mentoring.

Eligibility and Requirements

Academic and research preparation
CriterionRequirement
Academic preparationMasters or equivalent in (applied) physics or engineering, with a deep understanding of quantum physics.
Core qualitiesCurious and self-motivated, with strong interest in rare-earth ion physics and single emitters.
Valued experienceHands-on experience with quantum optics experiments, finite-element simulations, nanofabrication and cryogenics.
Cover letterMaximum one A4 page explaining motivation for working on single photon emitters and rare-earth ions; personally written letters are valued over AI-generated text.

Application Dates

Recruitment information
ComponentDetails
StatusOpen when checked on 22 October 2026
Deadline8 November 2026
Start dateNot specified
LocationDelft, Netherlands

How to Apply

Apply online through the official vacancy page with a CV (clearly stating any experience with nanofabrication, cryogenics, quantum optics and/or simulations) and a motivation letter of at most one A4 page. Applications sent by email or post are not processed.

About the Department

The Department of Quantum Nanoscience at TU Delft is a collaborative environment focused on quantum theory, quantum information science and quantum devices and materials, supported by state-of-the-art cleanroom facilities for realising next-generation nanostructures. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to learn new experimental techniques and to supervise Master students.

Official Sources

  • Official advert and application (verified link)
  • All current vacancies at TU Delft (official careers portal)

English language requirements

No IELTS or TOEFL certificate is requested for this employed Dutch position; English is assessed through the application documents and an interview in English.

Contact

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be raised through the contact channel given on the official announcement page (see the Official Link section above). Always quote the position reference in your message so the admissions or HR team can route your enquiry quickly.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: 8 November 2026 - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.
